card.name: Spots just before a line break
card.fires_on: Fires on a word or punctuation mark where the text is likely to continue after a break, such as a sentence-ending period before a section number, the CL in creatinine clearance, or a unit like mcg or per. It is most common in dosing and renal-impairment passages from flattened label text.

modes.label: Sentence-end period
modes.description: A period closing a sentence just before a new section or heading starts.
modes.example: discontinue naproxen tablets and naproxen sodium tablets and evaluate the patient immediately<<.>> 5.11 Fetal Toxic

modes.label: Creatinine clearance abbreviation
modes.description: The CL or Cl of CLcr inside a renal-impairment parenthesis.
modes.example: Patients with severe renal impairment (<<CL>> cr of <30 mL/min)

modes.label: Dose unit pieces
modes.description: A unit piece such as g in mcg or per in a dose rate within a dosing table.
modes.example: BELBUCA 75 mc<<g>> once daily or every 12 hours

card.writes: It lowers the chance that a plain newline comes next and favors table, bold or code-style line endings instead.
card.plain: It marks places in dosing text where a sentence, unit or table cell is about to continue, rather than ending the line.
